name: Nord & DeMaio
website: nord-demaio.com (now serves unrelated Chinese-language gambling content - domain lost or hijacked); current site is https://www.nordlaw.legal/
what_they_do: Business-oriented law firm now trading as NordLaw, representing companies in commercial litigation, construction, contracts, collections, and trademark/copyright matters. Same East Brunswick office at 190 State Highway 18, Suite 201.
customers: Small and mid-sized businesses, contractors, creditors and property owners - B2B clients rather than consumers.

size_signals.signal: 'Nearly 40 years' of experience stated on the site
Attorney profiles for Michael Nord, Michael Stafford and Adam Nord
Single East Brunswick office (Metroplex, 190 NJ-18 Suite 201) on Google, described as 'Legal services'

website_review.trust_signals: Almost none - no case results, no reviews, no credentials, no photos of the team
website_review.out_of_date_signs: The domain in every directory (nord-demaio.com) now serves an unrelated gambling site; the live Wix site is a thin brochure with placeholder-style icon graphics and 'copy-of-attorneys' / 'copy-of-practice-areas' URLs
website_review.search_basics: Home page title is 'Attorney | NordLaw | United States' - no service or town; practice areas exist only as a duplicated Wix page
top_issues: The old domain now serves gambling content, so directory traffic and link equity go to a hijacked page - a reputational and trust problem
Mobile layout is not responsive: page renders at a fixed 980px, cutting off navigation and hero text
No contact form, no practice-area detail, no proof of results - a business client cannot evaluate the firm online

agent_readiness.notes: Findable: claimed Google profile with hours, phone and website under the new NordLaw name, but the listing and all directories still carry the old name/domain; robots.txt is open (only blocks PetalBot and SEO crawlers). Answerable: almost no descriptive text - three value paragraphs, no case types with detail, no schema beyond default Wix output. Bookable: no form and no booking; 'Call Today' is the only route.

operations_signals.signal: Collections/contracts practice implies repetitive demand letters and invoice follow-up that is still manual (inference from practice areas)
Only two Google reviews at 3.0 while the firm has nearly 40 years of B2B work - no systematic review capture
No web intake at all, so each new commercial matter starts with a phone call and manual conflict check (inference)

top_opportunities.opportunity: Recover the brand: rebuild a proper NordLaw site on a new, owned domain and clean up every directory that still points at the lost nord-demaio.com
top_opportunities.evidence: nord-demaio.com returns unrelated gambling content; live site is a 3-page Wix brochure at copy-of-* URLs

top_opportunities.opportunity: Mobile-responsive rebuild with service pages for construction, collections and commercial litigation plus an enquiry form
top_opportunities.evidence: Fixed 980px layout on a 390px viewport, nav and hero text cut off; no form on any page

top_opportunities.opportunity: B2B intake and conflict-check workflow with automated engagement-letter generation for collections matters
top_opportunities.evidence: No web intake; practice mix is high-volume collections and contract work

scores.reasons: Gap: hijacked old domain, non-responsive site, no form, thin content, 3.0 rating. Pay: business-litigation clients pay well, but a three-lawyer shop with two reviews suggests limited scale. Ease: small firm, clear scope, though domain recovery adds work. Evidence: domain behaviour, live site, mobile rendering and listing all checked directly.
